A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AV-Link, with matching authors, core architecture and experiments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original V2A and A2V benchmark results, user studies and component ablations in Tables 1–4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains original AV-Link experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons and a 500-video analysis of MMDiffusion outputs.

M1.justification: The frozen backbones, Fusion Blocks, symmetric reinjection, temporal RoPE and objectives remain unchanged. The evaluated video pipeline now includes a described MAGVIT-v2 latent upsampler producing 512×288 video at 24 FPS. v1 evaluated native 36×64 outputs and described 144×256 upsampling only for demonstrations, making this a limited output-pipeline extension.

E1.justification: The training sources and principal VGGSound and Movie Gen evaluations remain unchanged. v2 adds a Landscapes-based diagnostic of MMDiffusion and briefly reports testing joint audio-video generation with AV-Link. Other datasets listed in Appendix D.3 describe prior work rather than additional evaluations conducted here.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 substantially broaden the V2A comparisons by adding Frieren and V2A-Mapper to automatic evaluation and user studies. v1 only described a website comparison with Frieren and cited V2A-Mapper in related work. Conversely, Table 2 removes MetaCLIP from the conditioning-feature comparison. The A2V comparator remains TempoTokens.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes generated-video evaluation from native 36×64 resolution to 512×288, materially changing the A2V evaluation setting. Appendix D.3 introduces a 500-video nearest-training-video CLIP comparison. Table 1 also stops reporting CLAP for unprompted cases. The principal test-set sizes, two-second A2V crop and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds the MMDiffusion memorization diagnostic and brief qualitative findings about joint AV-Link generation and RGB versus latent video models. It removes the MetaCLIP ablation row and the appendix's additional A2V example collection. Most timestep, block-placement, feature-injection and noise-scheduler analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify a single fixed evaluation seed for the ablations and five annotators per sample pair. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Revised averages and preference percentages do not establish a change in statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds baseline results and changes FoleyCrafter Onset ACC from 0.166/0.179 to 0.285/0.307 without/with prompts. Table 3 and A2V user preferences are revised: prompted AV-Link FID/FVD changes from 32.90/228.68 to 37.62/158.71 under the changed resolution, so these are replacement results rather than same-setting gains. v2 also reports 0.825 mean nearest-training-video CLIP similarity for MMDiffusion and removes MetaCLIP results.

T1.justification: The flow-matching equations, temporal RoPE definition, temporal alignment function and identity argument at conditioning timestep t=1 are retained. The added empirical observations and explanatory prose introduce no new proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The unified framework and diffusion-feature conditioning contributions remain unchanged. The introduction revises the headline Onset ACC advantage from 36.5 percentage points to 76.4% relative improvement against the updated baseline evidence. This changes the claimed performance margin without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds reasons for choosing a small RGB backbone and expands the discussion of paired-data scalability, restricted domains and apparent memorization in joint generators. Section 4.4 corrects the statement that static features outperform reinjection to underperform, agreeing with the retained Table 2. Existing scaling and inference-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the MAGVIT-v2 upsampler, initialization from the video model, 25,000 training iterations, batch size 384 and hardware. Table 1 newly identifies evaluations using released code/checkpoints versus author-provided outputs. Most optimizer, backbone, sampling and runtime details were already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the new Appendix D.3 expand the existing positioning against joint audiovisual generators, emphasizing data scalability and checkpoint/domain restrictions. New references include Ishii et al., Panda-70M, MAGVIT-v2 and additional concurrent V2A work. The central novelty positioning remains intact; Frieren and V2A-Mapper were already cited.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the related-work and method exposition are rewritten. Contribution bullets become an integrated narrative, feature reinjection receives expanded explanation, ablation topics are reordered, and Appendix D replaces its additional A2V subsection with joint-generation baseline discussion. These constitute substantial narrative editing despite the retained main section framework.

P2.justification: Figure 5 replaces its A2V examples, while Figure 8 replaces the additional A2V grid with MMDiffusion/generated-versus-training frame comparisons. Tables 1, 2 and 4 change row structure or explanatory notes, and several displays move. The two-column layout, architecture diagrams and principal diagnostic plots remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the comparative evidence with Frieren and V2A-Mapper evaluations, documents the evaluated upsampling pipeline, and corrects the reinjection explanation to match Table 2. These improve completeness and internal consistency. The gain is limited by removal of the MetaCLIP ablation and additional A2V examples; revised A2V scores also reflect changed evaluation resolution rather than demonstrated same-setting performance gains.
